purpose: Test whether the released SEPNET-PRISM hybrid sequence/tabular architecture can outperform the current IRIS late-fusion candidate when both are trained and scored on the exact IRIS NEW-crossing cohort.
target_semantics: Eligible only when >=10 pfu is not active at issue time; positive only when a new >=10 pfu operational event begins in the next 24 h.

cohort.score_role_note: 2023-2025 public development monitor already inspected; not fresh final evidence.

predictors.policy: Use the exact causal numeric FULL_CONTEXT columns from the IRIS public benchmark; exclude all Future_* columns and retrospective OSEP/GSEP catalogue labels.
predictors.equal_information_note: This gives the released architecture access to the same causal feature table as the IRIS full-context/late-fusion development models rather than restricting it to an easier subset.

sequence.history_rule: Input history must be strictly earlier than the target issue time; labels from non-fit roles are never used for fitting.

training.optuna_reason: Use the released fixed architecture/training recipe without post-result hyperparameter search on the already-inspected development monitor.

evaluation.calibration: logit intercept fitted on calibration role only
evaluation.paired_bootstrap_unit: complete SEP episode / predeclared quiet block

claim_rule: Do not call this an exact reproduction of the paper's reported random-IID result. It is a same-cohort reproduction of the released SEPNET-PRISM architecture and fixed training recipe under the stricter IRIS chronological NEW-crossing benchmark. No external superiority claim unless the paired interval clears zero and the comparator provenance audit passes.
